title: Train driver
change: Occupational standard and assessment plan revised
overviewOfRole: Train Drivers are responsible for driving trains in a safe, punctual, economic manner over various routes.
entryRequirements: <p>Individual employers must meet minimum requirements set by the Train Driving Licences and Certificates Regulations 2010; due to the nature of the role candidates must meet medical standards of physical health these are set out within the above regulations. To enter into an apprenticeship scheme the minimum age of a train driver is 17 years 6 months.</p>

knowledges.detail: Health and safety legislation and statutory operating regulations relevant to own role and organisation: industry procedures, safety requirements and instructions. Where and how to access information about changes to legislation and regulations.
Requirements and processes for ensuring rail safety and security on or near the line, trains and at stations and depots both locally, methods to report unsafe practice and including PREVENT protocol.
Regulation applicable to rail operation, licensing and certification of train drivers.

Procedures and methods for transfer of information across both internal and external stakeholders: report forms, radio protocol and communications equipment identification including emergency, lineside, level crossing and signal post telephones. Global System Mobile Communications – Railways (GSM-R) operating principles.
Impact of non-technical skills on safe, efficient rail services.
Organisational procedures for the response and management of operational incidents and emergencies during degraded and emergency working, within limits of own responsibility.
Specific professional and personal demands of the role, including fatigue management, shift work and personal wellbeing.
The range of traction types within own area of responsibility, the procedures for bringing trains in and out of service and shunting operations.
Procedures following identification of faults or hazards.
Introduction to and the importance of route learning.
Dangerous goods relevant to own role and organisation. Organisational procedures for action and reporting of dangerous goods in an emergency.
Special operational conditions and requirements relevant to your role.
The rail industry passenger and freight organisations, i.e. rail transport undertakings and other organisations, for example, regulatory body.
Techniques for maintaining personal competencies and supporting continuous professional development.
Environmental and sustainability regulations and guidance; environmental hazards that can arise from train operations. Equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) policies.
Verbal and written communication techniques; giving and receiving information; adapting style to audience.

behaviours.detail: Acts professionally, shows commitment and demonstrates robust ethics.
Demonstrates resilience and manages pressure well.
Safety first mindset, confident to challenge poor practice.
Demonstrates the ability to reflect and consistently self appraise their own performance to improve.
Supports environmental sustainability in the railway environment.
Seeks to support business goals and maintain an awareness of economic challenges
Collaborate with others to support colleagues and deliver train services.

skills.detail: Monitor own area of responsibility to ensure compliance with rail legislation, regulation and organisation procedures.
Demonstrate safe working, recognise and challenge unsafe practice according to organisational procedures.
Maintain a secure environment and respond to security issues in line with organisational procedures
Communicate information about the train or journey to internal or external audiences using the appropriate method during normal, degraded and emergency situations.
Apply critical thinking to assess situations and make informed, timely decisions that support safe operations.
Follow degraded working and emergency working procedures in the event of an incident.
Manage demands of the role including fatigue and personal wellbeing to sustain safe, efficient rail services.
Demonstrate practical handling of your traction types within your own responsibility to the standard required including on mainline and or depots and sidings.
Diagnose and resolve problems within own area of responsibility.
Start trains from different locations and under different circumstances e.g. Driver only operated services and guard operated services from stations and yards.
Learn and memorise route features within timescales including stations, signal types, junctions, tunnels, line speed.
Manage dangerous goods situations in own area of competency; report and protect other lines in a dangerous goods emergency.
Identify, adapt and comply with operational conditions: traction types and formation, speed restrictions, route availability, heavy axle weight, low adhesion.
Manage speed, braking and handling to optimise fuel economy, maintenance intervention and timetable adherence.
Carry out and record planned and unplanned CPD activities, evaluating against planned personal and professional development goals.
Follow procedures in line with environmental and sustainability regulations, standards and guidance; apply equity, diversity and inclusion (EDI) policies.
Communicate with others using appropriate methods for the audience.

reviewDetails: this apprenticeship will be reviewed in accordance with our change request policy.
clusterDescription: Drive a vehicle (road and rail) and provide routine support services

duties.dutyDetail: Comply with legislation and statutory operating regulations throughout the turn of duty.
Continuously monitor own area of responsibility to ensure compliance with rail legislation and organisational procedures, taking responsibility for maintaining personal competency.
Drive the train in line with organisational requirements.
Liaise with customers and/or other stakeholders to ensure an efficient train service.
Recognise and adapt to planned/degraded working conditions, mitigating risk.
Respond to emergencies/incidents in accordance with appropriate procedures.
Contribute to the commercial success of own organisation through meeting key performance indicators.
Complete all necessary reporting (in normal, degraded and emergency circumstances).
Manage own health and well-being to ensure compliance with train driver requirements.
